events.title: Trinity Kills the Cops; the Agents Arrive
events.summary: Four officers breach Room 303 of the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity under guns at her keyboard; she complies slowly, then, the instant the Big Cop reaches to cuff her, moves inhumanly fast and kills the entire squad, ending as the only one standing. Simultaneously, three suited Agents arrive outside, override the Lieutenant's territorial protest, and inform him his two units are already dead; Brown then enters the hotel while Smith breaks off alone for the alley.
events.action: The police breach and hold Trinity under guns with cuffs drawn; she submits, then converts the Big Cop's cuffing reach into a massacre, leaving every officer dead. Outside, the Agents arrive, correct the Lieutenant's belief that his men are bringing her down, and split the pursuit — Brown taking the building, Smith heading for the alley alone.

events.title: Trinity's Escape to the Phone
events.summary: Trinity's planned exit collapses when Morpheus reports the hardline is cut and Agents are on-site, so she is redirected to a phone at Wells and Lake and must fight her way out. She slips past Agent Brown in the hall, is forced up the fire escape by Agent Smith below, and crosses the rooftops where the pursuing cops' ordinary physics is shattered by her leap and by Agent Brown matching it. She dives through a distant window into a stairwell, confirms no Agent followed, and reaches the street where she races a garbage truck to answer the ringing booth at Wells and Lake an instant before it is destroyed. Left with wreckage, the Agents learn the informant is real and the crew's next target is Neo, and they launch a search.

events.title: Neo Is Summoned and Warned
events.summary: Across Neo's apartment and a crowded goth flat, an unseen party hijacks his computer to send him a series of messages that culminate in 'Follow the white rabbit,' and a planted white-rabbit pin flips his refusal into compliance; at the destination, Trinity names him, confirms she was on his machine, warns him that he is watched and in danger, and converts his private obsession into a named quest ('What is the Matrix?') before vanishing into the crowd. Neo moves from asleep-and-ordinary to shaken, his trust in cause-and-effect cracked so that he can only voice the breach as a question about being awake or dreaming; he still tries to perform the unflappable dealer but leaves that competent, controlled criminal normalcy in pieces, recruited rather than merely informed and with far less agency than he believes.
events.action: To break Neo's passive isolation and set him in motion toward the resistance by blurring the digital and the real, so that both he and the audience begin to distrust the solidity of his world at the very moment the Agents close in on his name.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Across Neo's apartment and a crowded goth flat, an unseen party hijacks his computer to send him a series of messages that culminate in 'Follow the white rabbit,' and a planted white-rabbit pin flips his refusal into compliance; at the destination, Trinity names him, confirms she was on his machine, warns him that he is watched and in danger, and converts his private obsession into a named quest ('What is the Matrix?') before vanishing into the crowd. Neo moves from asleep-and-ordinary to shaken
prose_before_reconcile.action: To break Neo's passive isolation and set him in motion toward the resistance by blurring the digital and the real, so that both he and the audience begin to distrust the solidity of his world at the very moment the Agents close in on his name.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The white-rabbit pin—the literal fulfillment of 'Follow the white rabbit'—which converts Neo's firm refusal into compliance and turns a drug deal into an abduction-by-invitation.

events.title: Neo's Capture at the Office
events.summary: Neo's ordinary morning collapses in a single run: a reprimand from his manager over lateness is instantly overwritten by a Federal Express delivery containing a ringing phone, through which Morpheus warns him that forces are closing in. Guided turn-by-turn, Neo slips past an Agent-led police search of the cubicle maze, but the one escape Morpheus offers — a scaffold and ledge to the roof — proves beyond his nerve; he breaks, climbs back inside, and is taken — handcuffed, head forced down, and driven off in a dark sedan under the Agents' control, as Trinity watches from her motorcycle.
events.action: An alarm drags Neo awake to a time that alarms him; his manager delivers an ultimatum about his job that Neo meets with flat, surface compliance. A courier hands him a softpak containing a phone that rings in his grip; Morpheus names the threat and directs his escape through the cubicle labyrinth while Agents and cops sweep the floor. Neo reaches an empty office and is ordered onto an exterior scaffold; he refuses, commits, then breaks when the wind hits and the phone falls, climbing back inside as a cop enters the room. Outside, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo to a dark sedan while Trinity watches from her motorcycle and reacts with dismay.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo's ordinary morning collapses in a single run: a reprimand from his manager over lateness is instantly overwritten by a Federal Express delivery containing a ringing phone, through which Morpheus warns him that forces are closing in. Guided turn-by-turn, Neo slips past an Agent-led police search of the cubicle maze, but the one escape Morpheus offers — a scaffold and ledge to the roof — proves beyond his nerve; the wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and climbs back inside, and is
prose_before_reconcile.action: An alarm drags Neo awake to a time that alarms him; his manager delivers an ultimatum about his job that Neo meets with flat, surface compliance. A courier hands him a softpak containing a phone that rings in his grip; Morpheus names the threat and directs his escape through the cubicle labyrinth while Agents and cops sweep the floor. Neo reaches an empty office and is ordered onto an exterior scaffold; he refuses, commits, then breaks when the wind hits and the phone falls, climbing back inside as a cop enters the room. Outside, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo to a dark sedan while Trinity watches from her motorcycle and reacts to what she sees.

events.title: The Interrogation and the Bug
events.summary: The event opens on Neo held in a white interrogation room, watched through a camera monitor as the Agents enter. Agent Smith lays out Neo's two lives from a manila file and offers to wipe his crimes clean in exchange for help locating Morpheus. Neo refuses with contempt, gives Smith the finger, and demands his phone call and his rights. Smith drops the negotiator's manner, asks what use a phone call is without speech, and Neo's mouth seals shut. When Neo lunges for the door the standing Agents pin him to the chair while Smith animates a fiber-optic wire tap into an insect-worm creature that burrows into Neo's navel, leaving Neo mouthless, implanted, and wholly under the Agents' control.
events.action: In a white interrogation room observed through a camera monitor, Agent Smith sits across from the captive Neo and presents a file documenting his double life as Thomas A. Anderson and the hacker Neo, then offers to erase his crimes if he helps capture Morpheus. Neo rejects the bargain with open insult — giving Smith the finger and demanding his phone call and his rights. Smith puts his glasses back on, declares his disappointment, and asks what good a phone call is if Neo cannot speak; Neo's jaw tightens, his lips seal shut until his mouth is gone, and when he lunges for the door the standing Agents pin him to the chair while Smith animates a fiber-optic wire tap into an insect-worm creature that burrows into Neo's navel.

events.title: Neo Chooses to Meet Morpheus
events.summary: Jolted out of bed by the ringing phone, Neo is told by Morpheus that he is 'the One' and that Morpheus has spent his life searching for him, leaving him sick and unsettled; he commits to the meeting and is instructed to go to the Adams Street bridge. On the rain-soaked street Trinity pulls up and he is seized and forced into a moving car, where Switch holds him at gunpoint and Trinity produces a steel-and-glass device for a procedure 'for our protection. From you.' Ignorant of why he is restrained, Neo is told only that the danger is himself and is reminded of a road he already knows; after cornered defiance and an impulse to flee, he opens the car door and then closes it, choosing to stay as the car rushes off through the wet underworld.
events.action: The ringing phone forces Neo out of bed; he answers '... Yes,' committing to meet Morpheus and accepting the instruction to go to the Adams Street bridge. On the street Trinity pulls up; Neo is grabbed and held at gunpoint in a moving car, where Switch keeps the gun trained on him and Trinity produces the steel-and-glass device. Neo moves to bolt, opening the car door, but the reminder of the road he already knows and the claim that the threat is himself turn his resistance into self-destruction; he closes the door and stays, and the car carries them off through the wet underworld. Switch ends any negotiation by stopping the car and laying down the group's one rule.

events.title: Arrival at the Lafayette and the Choice
events.summary: The crew's car sheds its trail in the rainy night and halts in the deserted alley behind the Hotel Lafayette. Trinity escorts Neo to room 1313 and, before handing him off, advises him to be honest because whoever waits inside knows more than he can possibly imagine. Morpheus reveals himself and redirects Neo's hero-worship toward the nameless wrongness he has felt his whole life, then defines the Matrix as an illusory prison for the mind that can only be seen, not explained. Offered an irreversible choice, Neo swallows the red pill, committing to the truth with no going back, and Morpheus becomes the guide who will show him what he has chosen.
events.action: The bug is dumped from the car and reverts to a wire tap as the vehicle breaks contact and vanishes into the rainy night, then halts in the deserted alley behind the Hotel Lafayette. Trinity leads Neo to room 1313 and, before delivering him to Morpheus, tells him to be honest because the man inside knows more than he can possibly imagine. Morpheus reveals himself, welcomes Neo, and steers him past hacker hero-worship toward the lifelong unease he carries, then defines the Matrix as an illusory prison for the mind that cannot be explained, only seen. He stages a final choice between two pills; Neo swallows the red pill, committing to the truth, and Morpheus tells him to follow.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's voluntary swallowing of the red pill licenses everything that follows — the trace program that unplugs him, the horror of the pod and the atrophied body, and his entry into the real world as Morpheus's recruit. Because he chose, the catastrophe reads as
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It ends Neo's ordinary life and any return to it — 'no going back' — and forecloses Switch's preferred reading of Neo as a mere liability, since Morpheus has now secured him as the One.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The bug's reversion to a common wire tap on the pavement means the Agents' tap on Neo is severed, which the pursuing machine-side will register as a lost signal — a fact the scenes do not show but the extraction makes true.

events.turns_on: The red pill — not the extraction, not the warning, but Neo's own swallow — is the pivot: every prior beat exists to bring him to a choice he must make for himself, and the moment he commits, with no going back, the event's whole direction locks.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: The crew's car slips away through the rain and stops behind the decaying Hotel Lafayette. Trinity leads Neo to room 1313, warning him to be honest because whoever waits inside 'knows more than you can possibly imagine,' then hands him to Morpheus. In a rotting room, Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong unease as evidence of a hidden enslaving system — the Matrix — and offers an irreversible choice between a blue pill of comfortable ignorance and a red pill of truth. Neo swallows the red pill, and is
prose_before_reconcile.action: The bug is dumped from the car and reverts to a wire tap as the vehicle vanishes into the rainy night, then halts in a deserted alley behind the Hotel Lafayette. Trinity escorts Neo to room 1313 on the thirteenth floor and, before handing him off, advises him to be honest because 'she warns that he knows far more than Neo could ever imagine.' Morpheus reveals himself, welcomes Neo, and steers him past hacker hero-worship toward the nameless wrongness he has felt his whole life. When Neo names 'The Matrix,' Morpheus defines it as an illusory prison for the mind that cannot be explained, only seen, and stages a final choice between two pills. Neo swallows the red pill, committing to the truth, and Morpheus tells him to follow.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The red pill — not the extraction, not the warning, but Neo's own swallow — is the pivot: every prior beat exists to bring him to a choice he must make for himself, and the moment his throat works the event's whole direction locks.

events.title: Tracing Neo Out of the Matrix
events.summary: The crew turns Morpheus's philosophy into a physical extraction: while Apoc hunts for Neo's signal under mounting pressure, the trace program dissolves Neo's body through the mirror and drives him into cardiac arrest, and only at the last instant does the lock land so Morpheus can fire. Neo falls out of the Matrix and wakes in a magenta pod inside an immense human power plant; he claws free bald and naked, sees the endless ranks of farmed bodies, and is disconnected by a machine that then flushes him through the waste system. A cable hauls him half-conscious into the hovercraft, where he is dropped onto the floor, helped upright, and looks straight at Morpheus before passing out.
events.action: Morpheus conducts the extraction while running his dream/reality lesson in parallel, timing crew commands around Neo's dissolution and breaking into urgency only when the monitors scream; Apoc reports 'Still nothing' under repeated pressing, then lands a clean lock ('Lock! I got him!') exactly as Neo arrests, letting Morpheus fire the signal; Trinity narrows from a single nod to clinical readings, reporting Neo going into arrest rather than comforting him; Cypher deflects with a joke ('buckle up, Dorothy') and returns to his data; Switch holds her station without a line; Neo is unmade by the mirror-liquid, dragged through arrest and darkness, wakes in a pod, discovers the coaxial cable locked into the base of his skull and the field of human batteries, is disconnected and flushed through the waste lines, and is hauled half-conscious into the hovercraft where Morpheus names him and 'the real world' before he passes out.

affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It burns the crew's position inside the Matrix — the trace and the near-fatal arrest mean the room, the ship's connection, and their method are now exposed and compromised, forcing them to move. It costs Neo any remaining innocence about the price of 'the real
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents and the Matrix's enforcement apparatus register the anomaly of a freed battery and the trace signal, setting the pursuit in motion off-screen; inside the ship, Tank — named but unseen — receives Morpheus's call and stands ready to take the wheel

events.turns_on: The event pivots on whether Neo can be located and pulled free before his own body gives out — the whole extraction, and the philosophy made flesh, hangs on a signal lock arriving one beat ahead of death.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Neo survives the arrest or what exactly lies in the darkness he is swallowed into.
Whether the mirror's liquefaction is a physical event in the room or a manifestation inside Neo's perception of the Matrix.
What 'Tank' and 'the signal' concretely are beyond Morpheus's call for them.
Whether the machine's disconnection of Neo is meant to free him or to harvest him.
Where the black hole sucks Neo to.
Whether the human hands and arms belong to crew members or to Morpheus.
Whether Neo's passing out is from exhaustion or the transition to the real world.

events.boundary_reason: The question shifts to 'How do they physically locate and extract Neo's body?' — the trace program, the mirror-liquid invasion, the pod awakening, the fall through the waste lines, and the rescue into the hovercraft are one continuous extraction ending when Morpheus welcomes him to the real world and he passes out.

prose_before_reconcile.action: Morpheus conducts the extraction while running his dream/reality lesson in parallel, timing crew commands around Neo's dissolution; Apoc hunts for the target lock under lethal pressure and lands it just as Neo arrests, letting Morpheus fire the signal; Trinity monitors Neo's failing vitals and reports the crisis rather than comforting him; Cypher deflects with a joke and returns to his data; Switch holds her station without a line; Neo is unmade by the mirror-liquid, dragged through arrest and darkness, wakes in a pod, discovers the coaxial in his skull and the field of human batteries, is disconnected and flushed through the waste lines, and is hauled half-conscious into the hovercraft where Morpheus welcomes him before he passes out.

events.title: Recovery and Reorientation
events.summary: Neo is pulled from the sewer and wakes aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, where Morpheus—certain they have found the one they sought, against Trinity's caution—has his atrophied body rebuilt through needles and pain while steadying his frightened, half-conscious mind with small doses of truth. As Neo wakes to foreign hardware grafted into his own flesh, Morpheus refuses to explain and instead reframes him in time: it is not 1997 but near 2197, a revelation that knocks the wind from him. Morpheus then converts explanation into an act of showing, leading the sleepwalking Neo through the ship, naming it as his home, toward the main deck.
events.action: retrieving Neo to show him reality rather than explain it, rebuilding his body, and leading him like a sleepwalker toward the main deck

events.title: The Truth of the Matrix
events.summary: Morpheus performs a ritual he has done before, guiding Neo through staged revelations on a television while keeping his own voice clinical. He moves from abstract framing (the scorched sky, dependence on machines) through the specific horror (humans farmed, grown in fields, the dead liquefied to feed the living) to the terminal symbol (a human being reduced to a coppertop battery), and in retelling his own conversion from disbelief to certainty reaffirms the horrifying precision of the system. Neo is jacked in, transported into weightlessness, and subjected to the revelation; at each widening he reaches for a stable definition and resists, his grasp turning to panic, until the truth becomes unbearable and his whole organism revolts — he thrashes against the coaxial line, is restrained by Dozer while Trinity works the cable, is freed, and collapses, vomiting and blacking out as his body rejects what his mind refuses to accept. Trinity treats the reaction as a known pattern, offering procedural comfort while holding a private stake in him. Cypher reads the catastrophe bluntly as a body reaching its limit ('He's going to pop!'). Mouse, Tank, and Dozer are present as the crew arrayed for the initiation but act or speak little on the page.
events.action: Morpheus jacks Neo into the Construct and stages a sequence of revelations on a television — the simulated city, the scorched sky, the fetus fields, the power plant, and finally the coppertop battery — narrating with clinical detachment and recounting his own conversion. Neo is helped into one of six ecto-skeleton chairs, has the coaxial line fired into the socket at the base of his neck, and is pulled into weightlessness. As each image widens the category of what is real, he resists and demands release; when the battery is revealed his mind refuses it and his body revolts on the ship. He thrashes against the cable, is held down while Trinity works the line free, and then collapses, vomiting and blacking out.

events.title: The Prophecy of the One
events.summary: Neo, raw and half-dissolved by what he was shown and by his body's physical rejection of a reality his mind will not accept, asks from resignation whether he can go back; Morpheus answers no. Morpheus, steadying himself as much as Neo, apologizes for breaking the rule against freeing an older mind, then recounts the origin myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy, closing with his conviction that 'the search is over' and the promise of Neo's training. Neo receives the prophecy passively, his rescue reframed as the object of a lifelong search; Morpheus, transmuting guilt into grandeur, steps fully into the role of mentor and true believer, his faith in Neo remaining a wager rather than a confirmed fact.

events.title: Loading the Skills
events.summary: Across a single continuous stretch on the main deck, Tank loads combat programs into Neo one after another—jujitsu first, then a ten-hour run of the combat series—converting Neo from a skillless prospect into a man who has combat knowledge downloaded straight into him. The first load shocks Neo into exhilarated belief, and the long run that follows collapses his disbelief into intoxicated certainty; he emerges from the final download declaring he knows kung fu. Morpheus arrives only to ask after him—'How is he?'—and, refusing to celebrate the claim, converts it into a test with his two-word demand: 'Show me.'

Tank loads combat programs into Neo; Neo moves from disbelief through bodily, almost ecstatic shock into thrilled ownership of the skills; after a long run of downloads he declares mastery; Morpheus arrives as an observer checking status, then moves from observer to instructor by refusing to let the self-report count until it is performed.

events.title: The Jump
events.summary: Morpheus demonstrates the rooftop jump and Neo attempts it, reading it as a feat he can force with effort; he falls drastically short, plummets, and is bounced to rest on his back, then is helped up by Morpheus and names his own disbelief as the cause. On the main deck the crew watches the attempt on a screen: Apoc and Tank rule the jump impossible on the record, Mouse holds open the possibility that Neo might be the exception, and Trinity physically wills him across.
events.action: Morpheus runs and leaps the gap to the far rooftop, crossing it effortlessly, then leaves the building to reach the fallen Neo. Neo braces to run, launches, comes up drastically short, plummets, and is bounced to rest on his back; Morpheus lifts him to his feet. On the main deck the crew watches on the screen: Apoc and Tank dismiss the jump on the record, Mouse keeps raising the possibility that Neo might succeed, and Trinity, breaking her reserve, clenches her fists and whispers for him to make it. Morpheus draws the reason out of Neo, who offers that he didn't think he would make it, and Morpheus nods.

events.title: The Agent Training Program
events.summary: Morpheus walks Neo through a crowded downtown street that is actually a training program, reframing the ordinary people inside the Matrix as part of the system and therefore the enemy. When Neo is distracted by a woman in a red dress, Morpheus turns the lapse into a lesson: the crowd can become an Agent, and a gun materializing at Neo's face makes him scream. Morpheus freezes the program and teaches that Agents are sentient programs able to inhabit anyone still plugged in, and that every human who has fought one has died — but Neo will succeed because Agents are bound by rules while Neo is not. Neo's question about dodging bullets is answered with 'when you're ready, you won't have to,' and the lesson breaks off when Morpheus' phone rings with Tank's report of trouble.
events.action: Morpheus uses the crowded downtown street as a training program to harden Neo, flattening the people they mean to save into 'the enemy.' events.title: The Sentinel Hunt
events.summary: The Nebuchadnezzar blisters through a sewer main, trailing a supercharged electromagnetic wake, then is ordered down and wedged into a supply line too small for it to hide from a sweeping Sentinel. In the cockpit the alarm interrupts Morpheus's check on the warning's source; Dozer reports the machine coming in and Morpheus orders the ship set down and hidden. Trinity and Dozer brief Neo on what a Sentinel is and why stillness is the only defense, while Morpheus stops Neo from moving with a warning that the machine hunts by sound. On the main deck the turbines die, power goes off-line, and Tank arms the E.M.P. and closes his fingers around the glowing red key. In the frozen cockpit the crew waits motionless while the machine glides over them and passes on; only once it is gone do they relax, and the ship settles into quiet and sleep.
events.action: The Nebuchadnezzar blisters through the sewer main trailing a swirling supercharged electromagnetic wake, then is squeezed down into a supply line barely its size and left wedged, hidden and motionless. In the cockpit the alarm snaps Morpheus from his inquiry about the warning's status into survival; Dozer is first to report a Sentinel sweeping in, and Morpheus orders the ship set down to hide. Neo, who does not know what a Squiddy is, is briefed by Trinity and Dozer that it is a search-and-destroy machine and that the E.M.P. is their only weapon, and when he angles to look, Morpheus grabs him with the warning that the machine hunts by sound and he freezes. On the main deck the turbines grind to a halt, Tank reports power off-line with the E.M.P. armed, and he curls his fingers around the small glowing red key. Back in the cockpit the heat dies and the crew huddles in the cold; Dozer wipes the frost from the windshield, they watch the machine glide over them and vanish, and once it has passed they breathe easier. The ship goes quiet and dark and everyone sleeps.

prose_before_reconcile.action: The Nebuchadnezzar blisters through the sewer main and then sets down, wedged nearly tight into a pipe too small for it. In the cockpit, an alarm interrupts Morpheus's check on the warning's source; Dozer reports a Sentinel sweeping in and Morpheus orders the ship hidden. Neo, ignorant of the threat, is briefed by Trinity and Dozer. On the main deck the turbines die, power goes off-line, and Tank arms the E.M.P. and grips the glowing key. Back in the cockpit the crew waits in silence as the heat fails and the cold sets in; Morpheus stops Neo from moving with a warning that the machine hunts by sound, Dozer clears the frost, and they watch the machine glide over them and vanish, after which the ship goes quiet and everyone sleeps.

events.title: Cypher's Doubt and His Deal
events.summary: On the main deck, Cypher isolates Neo at the operator's chair and, over Dozer's liquor, reframes Morpheus's prophecy as a lethal pattern that has already killed five would-be Ones, seeding Neo's doubt. That regret hardens off-screen into an open transaction: in an upscale restaurant inside the Matrix, Cypher agrees to deliver Morpheus to Agent Smith in exchange for being reinserted as a rich, important man who remembers nothing.
events.action: Cypher plays the worldly veteran on the deck, toasting with Neo and forcing him to take shots of Dozer's liquor, then steers the talk from homesick small talk into a systematic undermining of Morpheus — mocking the 'save the world' mandate and revealing that Morpheus has believed he found the One five times before, and that all five died taking on an Agent. Neo performs the willing crewmate, forcing down the shots until he is red-faced and coughing, and takes Cypher's warning as caution. The scene then cuts to a restaurant where Cypher savors a steak he knows is fake and finalizes a deal with Agent Smith: his body returned to a power plant and reinserted into the Matrix as someone rich and forgetful, in return for the access codes to the Zion mainframe. When Cypher offers 'the man who does,' Smith supplies the target himself: 'Morpheus.'

events.title: Approach to the Oracle
events.summary: A vast, tenement-like building is presented as a place where people can disappear, setting a hushed, clandestine register for the approach. Inside, Morpheus carries quiet, absolute conviction as he guides Neo, and during the elevator ascent Neo presses him with escalating questions about the Oracle — the prophecy, its beginning, whether she is ever wrong — trying to test the authority who will deliver a verdict about him. Morpheus reframes her as a fallible guide who 'knows enough' and cannot be judged in terms of right and wrong, then grounds his faith in the personal revelation that she told him she would find the One.
events.action: Neo follows Morpheus from standing in the building into the elevator and rises with him, carried upward toward the meeting.

events.title: Faith at the Door and the Lesson of the Spoon
events.summary: Two thresholds in sequence. In a dark hall, Morpheus reaches the limit of what a guide can do—he can only show the door—so he stops arguing doctrine and offers Neo the one thing he has left: a confessed, hard-won faith. He admits he misread the Oracle, thought the prophecy was about him, and was terribly wrong about the five before Neo; then he asks Neo only to lean on residual respect and trust him until Neo feels what he felt. Neo, who has been resisting and pulling back from the door and insisting he does not believe, is moved by Morpheus's confessed faith and commits to stepping through, answering Morpheus's plea for trust with agreement. events.title: The Oracle's Verdict
events.summary: In the Oracle's kitchen, the old woman performs harmless fussiness so completely that Neo drops his guard, then dismantles his skepticism with a vase she predicts and reframes as his own choice, a physical exam, and a two-dose prophecy before telling him plainly he is not the One but is 'waiting for something.' She then delivers the real blow: Morpheus believes in him so absolutely he will die to save him, and Neo will hold the choice of which of them lives. The death-prophecy seizes his throat as somatic panic, which the Oracle soothes back to calm with reassurance and a cookie that works exactly as she promised. Led out silent, he nods acceptance as Morpheus, waiting outside, behaves as one who already knows a private verdict was delivered and offers to keep it secret.
events.action: The Oracle converts Neo from an ironic disbeliever into a young man carrying a lethal, personal choice — knowing he is not the One, knowing Morpheus will die for him unless he chooses otherwise, and no longer a bystander to Morpheus's faith — while loading him toward the rescue he will make in ev-026; Morpheus moves from presumed ignorance of the private audience to acting as though he knows its verdict and offering to keep it.

events.title: The Déjà Vu — 'It's a Trap'
events.summary: Climbing the Hotel Lafayette stairwell, Neo sees a black cat and then an identical second one; his casual 'deja vu' freezes the whole crew dead. In the real world the Nebuchadnezzar's monitors seize at the same instant, and Tank recoils at the malfunction before reading what was changed on the main deck. Trinity interrogates Neo into confirming the repeat, then delivers the rule — a deja vu is a glitch that happens when 'they change something' — while Morpheus listens to the building's breath. Helicopter blades build outside, and Tank names the whole maneuver a trap.
events.action: A freed mind's throwaway observation becomes the crew's tripwire. Neo's civilian reflex collides with operational reality, and the scene's work is the transfer of that knowledge: Trinity translating the glitch into a threat under fire, Morpheus reading the threat one layer beneath her through the building's rasping breath, and Tank, alone on the main deck, identifying the seizure as a deliberate ambush. The event folds a small eerie coincidence into the story's alarm bell.

events.title: The Ambush Springs — Mouse Dies
events.summary: The trap Tank identified closes in a single tightening motion. On the staircase the crew arms up while, below, an unknown hand severs the basement hardline with bolt cutters. Isolated in Room 1313, Mouse is drawn to the windows by the helicopter and warned by Tank that the hardline is cut and it is a trap — but the warning arrives only after the windows have already been rewritten into brick. He sees the bricked window, realises he is sealed in, and his involuntary 'Oh no' betrays the recognition before gunfire hurls him back against the glass and pins him there; his body thrashes once and goes still as the life monitor flatlines on the Nebuchadnezzar's deck. Morpheus, mid-ascent, is halted when Mouse's scream is swallowed by machine-gun fire; Tank can only watch and repeat 'No, no, no.'
events.action: The event is the trap's execution and its first crew casualty. It converts the abstract dread of the Oracle's prophecy into concrete, irreversible cost, and proves the Matrix's own environment can be weaponised against the crew: the windows Mouse would have escaped through have been rewritten into brick, and the severed hardline destroys the crew's only remaining exit. With both routes gone, Mouse's death is made inescapable — the exit Tank assumes still exists is already destroyed before the warning reaches Mouse — so the crew's retreat is compromised as surely as their bodies.

events.title: The Escape Through the Walls
events.summary: The police convert the unsearched Hotel Lafayette into a methodical floor-by-floor sweep that closes on the eighth floor and uncovers the escape hole, while the trapped crew works by remote relay: Tank finds the structural drawing and then directs Morpheus blind through the rooms, and Morpheus arrives at Room 808 and names the main wet-wall as the way out. Agent Smith, standing over Mouse's body after the line clicks dead, reports the targets are on the eighth floor; the report passes up to Agent Brown in the stairwell as boots and cops ascend and flood the floor. The cops sweep the empty Room 808 and find only the man-sized hole in the bathroom wall, a beat after the crew has vanished into the plumbing wall to descend the grease-black stack pipes.
events.action: The police sweep the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor, turning the sealed building into an active search that reaches the eighth floor and finds the man-sized hole in Room 808's bathroom wall. On the ship, Tank locates the structural diagram and then the main wet-wall, relaying each to Morpheus and guiding his blind movement—telling him to go left, since the opening is now directly ahead—until Morpheus reaches the target room, where he dictates the main wet-wall as the crew's path out. Meanwhile Agent Smith, standing over Mouse's corpse, reaches his earpiece; when the line clicks dead he reports the targets are on the eighth floor, and that report passes to Agent Brown in the stairwell as boots clatter up the marble stairs and cops flood the floor and sweep the empty Room 808, finding only the hole—through which the crew has already slipped, worming down the grease-black stack pipes inside the plumbing wall.

events.title: The Cops Close In on the Wall
events.summary: In the hall, Agent Brown stands over Morpheus's abandoned jacket and, receiving a report through his earpiece, openly demands the location of the fugitives, with Agent Smith silent beside him. In Room 608, the cops comb in silence until one singles out a strange sound near the bathroom that the others have not noted. Inside the wall, Cypher has slipped and is stuck, pinned where the wall meets several thick supply pipes. In Room 608, a cop presses his ear to the plaster, straining to hear whispers, hisses and a grunt through it, and then the wall bulges and shatter-cracks, and he understands the fugitives are concealed inside the wall structure.
events.action: The hunt narrows from a general demand into a specific discovery. Agent Brown's open demand in the hall sends the search into Room 608, where the cops' silent combing gives way to one of them singling out a strange sound near the bathroom; pressing his ear closer, he strains to hear whispers, hisses and a grunt through the plaster, and the wall bulges and shatter-cracks, exposing that the fugitives are concealed inside the structure. The event runs in parallel across three spaces—the hall, Room 608, and the cavity of the wall—and the tension comes from the hunters and the hunted occupying the same structure without yet seeing one another.

events.title: Firefight in the Wall and Descent
events.summary: Trapped inside the wall, the crew turns a pinned-down ambush into a running escape: Neo returns fire, Trinity hauls Cypher out of the line of fire, and when an Agent breaches the wall and nearly throttles Neo, Morpheus dives the Agent and pins him, ordering Trinity to get Neo out because he is all that matters. Trinity—torn between the man she loves and the duty Morpheus imposes—overrules her own rescue instinct and drags the resisting Neo away, keeping a commander's narrowed focus through the basement firefight; she finds the catch-basin cover and pries the grate open, and the survivors descend into the wet-black hole. Cypher, pulled clear but lagging and watching rather than helping, 'seems to trip' as a gas can bounces near him and is swallowed by the gas smoke, lost and separated from the crew.
events.action: The Cop opens fire into the wall; Trinity hauls Cypher out of the line of fire and Neo finds his gun and blasts back through the plaster. The gunfire dies, then an Agent smashes through the wall and nearly collapses Neo's throat before Morpheus dives him to the floor and pins the Agent weaponless. Morpheus orders Trinity to take Neo out; over Neo's protests she grabs him and drags him away, and the group drops into the basement amid grenade fire. Trinity locates the catch-basin cover and pries the grate open, then follows the others down the wet-black hole. Cypher—watching her work—'seems to trip' as a gas can bounces near him and vanishes into the gas smoke, hidden and separated from the crew.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Trapped inside the wall, the crew turns a trapped-box ambush into a running escape: Neo returns fire, Trinity pulls Cypher clear, and when an Agent breaches the wall to kill Neo, Morpheus ambushes the Agent and pins him, ordering Trinity to get Neo out because 'he is all that matters.' Trinity obeys against her will and drags the protesting Neo away, abandoning Morpheus to the Agent; the survivors crash into the basement firefight, Trinity opens the catch-basin exit, and Cypher is swallowed by气体
prose_before_reconcile.action: The Cop opens fire into the wall; Trinity hauls Cypher out of the line of fire and Neo arms himself and blasts back through the plaster. The gunfire dies, then an Agent smashes through the wall and nearly throttles Neo before Morpheus dives him to the floor and pins him weaponless. Morpheus orders Trinity to take Neo out; she relays 'Go!' and, over Neo's protests, grabs his ankle and slides them both down the wall. The group drops into the basement amid grenade fire, Trinity pries open the catch-basin grate, and Cypher—watching her work—'seems to trip' and vanishes into gas smoke as the others descend.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Morpheus's decision to trade his own life for Neo's, converting a chaotic firefight into a moral crisis and launching the capture-and-rescue arc.

events.title: Morpheus Captured
events.summary: On the floor of Room 608, Smith pries Morpheus's strangling hands off his throat, absorbs a nose-and-glasses-shattering head-butt, and answers with three head-butts and a kick that drive Morpheus staggering into the wall. The moment his own grip fails, Smith stops relying on his body and reaches for the institution behind him, ordering the cops in the doorway to take Morpheus, who is buried under them. On the main deck, Tank watches the capture unfold on the screen, reaches out toward it, and cries 'No!' — the escape that succeeded for Neo and Trinity now registered off-site as the loss of the man they could not pull out.
events.action: Morpheus converts a fight he can no longer win into a single close-range strike meant to end it before the room fills, but his grip fails as Smith pries free and his spent head-butt buys nothing; three returned head-butts plus a kick drive him staggering into the wall before the cops overwhelm him, leaving him slammed against it and buried under a tide of cops. Smith, pinned and unable to breathe, pries the hands free, registers the nose-shattering head-butt as information rather than suffering, returns three head-butts, and drives Morpheus into the wall — and the instant his own body stops being enough, he reaches past it to the institution behind him, turning a losing duel into a police action by ordering the cops to take Morpheus. Tank, watching on the screen, reaches out as if he could reach Morpheus and cries 'No!' in helpless distress, his scene giving him no agency beyond witness.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: The one-on-one struggle on the floor of Room 608 ends decisively. Smith frees his throat despite a head-butt that shatters his nose and glasses, answers with three head-butts and a kick that drives Morpheus into the wall, then converts the fight into a police action by ordering the cops in the doorway to take him. Morpheus is buried under their numbers. On the main deck, Tank, watching on the screen, reaches out and cries out 'No!' — the crew's escape now registered off-site as a loss.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Morpheus spends his last leverage in a viper-strike head-butt to finish the strangling Agent, but Smith absorbs it and the injury only pushes him to reach past his own failing body toward the institution behind him. Smith frees his throat, returns three head-butts, and kicks Morpheus deep into the plaster, then commands the wall of cops to seize him; Morpheus disappears under them. The capture is witnessed remotely by Tank, whose helpless reach and cry close the escape as a defeat.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The pivot is the moment Smith's own grip fails and he stops relying on his body, reaching instead for the institution behind him — converting a duel he was losing into a police action.

events.title: Survivors Regroup
events.summary: Across two fronts the scattered crew re-establishes contact. Trinity forces a manhole cover open and climbs out onto the street, then reaches Tank by phone; Tank, alone at the monitors, identifies two callers in turn—Cypher, desperate for an exit, then Trinity—and routes both to Franklin and Erie. Cypher, steadied by the crash that has cleared his path, is given that exit and composes himself as fire trucks approach. Trinity relays Tank's confirmation that Morpheus is alive but being moved, and learns Cypher has been positioned at Franklin and Erie, so the crew is routed toward the one crewmate Trinity distrusts.
events.action: Trinity forces the manhole cover open and climbs out onto the street in daylight. Tank, alone at the monitors, takes a panicked call from Cypher, who reports a car accident and demands a fast exit; Tank routes him to Franklin and Erie. Trinity then reaches Tank and identifies herself, and, moving with Neo down a back street, asks about Morpheus; Tank confirms Morpheus is alive but being moved. Trinity demands an exit and learns Cypher has been positioned at Franklin and Erie, despite the crew's suspicion of him. Cypher, composed and self-satisfied, is given that same exit and waits as fire trucks approach.

events.title: The Dead Line
events.summary: A clean exit curdles into the crew's worst night. In the TV repair shop, the phone Neo answers goes dead, and Trinity's shift to the cellular reaches not the operator but Cypher, who reports that Tank 'had an accident.' On the main deck the lie is exposed: Cypher has murdered Dozer and Tank's chair, given Morpheus to the Agents, and is picking off the jacked-in crew—Apoc, then Switch—while Trinity argues, pleads, and finally, under threat to Neo, whispers 'yes' to Neo being the One. Tank, alive and wounded, answers Cypher's taunt for a miracle with a lightning bolt that drops him mid-sentence. Back in the shop, Trinity and Neo share a brief embrace before the ringing phone drives them out, Neo reversing their usual order and sending her first.
events.action: In the TV repair shop, Neo holds the ringing phone and then finds only dead silence; Trinity takes out the cellular and is answered by Cypher instead of the operator. Cypher reports that Tank 'had an accident' and, on the main deck, is revealed as the murderer of Dozer and Tank's chair who has given Morpheus to the Agents and is pulling the plug cables from the jacked-in crew—Apoc, then Switch. Trinity argues and pleads, and under threat to Neo's life whispers 'yes' to Neo being the One. Wounded and armed, Tank survives, fires the gun that shoots lightning, and drops Cypher mid-triumph. Trinity and Neo are physically reunited in the shop and share a brief embrace before the ringing phone forces them back out, with Neo telling her 'You first this time.'

affects_outside.enables: With the crew gutted and Morpheus gone, the story is cleared for the rescue arc: only Trinity and Neo remain to go back for Morpheus, and Trinity's affirmed belief in Neo as the One becomes the emotional engine for that mission.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The crew is reduced by three—Apoc and Switch murdered, Tank wounded and Cypher down—so the Nebuchadnezzar loses its operator capacity and Morpheus is delivered into the Agents' hands, closing off any clean escape and forcing a rescue instead.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, now holding Morpheus, will act on the prize Cypher delivered; their interrogation of Morpheus (and the ship's remaining crew reacting to the massacre) is set in motion beyond these scenes.

events.turns_on: The event pivots on whether the dead line means a mere malfunction or a betrayal—and the answer, delivered across the call and the deck, is that it is the latter: Cypher has turned on the crew, murdering Apoc and Switch, giving up Morpheus, and being stopped only by the Tank he believed dead.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: A clean exit curdles into the crew's worst night. In the TV repair shop, the phone Neo answers goes dead, and Trinity's shift to the cellular only reaches Cypher, who reports Tank 'had an accident.' On the main deck the lie is exposed: Cypher, having murdered Dozer and Tank's chair, has given Morpheus to the Agents and is picking off the jacked-in crew—Apoc, then Switch—while Trinity argues, pleads, and finally, under threat to Neo, whispers 'yes' to Neo being the One. prose_before_reconcile.action: Tank, alive and wounded, answers Cypher's taunt for a miracle with a lightning bolt that drops him mid-sentence. Back in the shop, Trinity and Neo share a brief embrace before the ringing phone drives them out, Neo reversing their usual order and sending her first.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The event pivots on whether the dead line means a mere malfunction or a betrayal—and the answer, delivered across the call and the deck, is that it is the latter: Cypher has turned on the crew.

events.title: Trinity Wakes to the Cost
events.summary: Trinity wakes on the ship, unplugged and reoriented to the ship's return, and measures the cost of her unconsciousness by reading it off Tank: his burns kill her relief at the ship's survival, and she reads Dozer's death from the tightening of Tank's face rather than having it spoken.
events.action: Trinity wakes and is unplugged; she observes Tank's burns, he offers her the kindness of downplaying his own wounds, and when she moves toward the subject of Dozer his face tightens and she completes the inference he will not voice.

events.title: Neo Chooses to Rescue Morpheus
events.summary: As Tank prepares to unplug the dying Morpheus to keep the ship's codes from the Agents, Neo's paralysis breaks and he stops him. Recalling the Oracle's warning that he would have to make a choice, Neo decides to jack back into the Matrix to rescue Morpheus. He tells Trinity he is not the One and that Morpheus died for a faith Neo now believes was mistaken, so Morpheus—not he—is what matters. Tank protests the plan.
events.action: Tank reaches for the plug to end Morpheus's life; Neo stops him and reverses the crew's momentum. He declares his intent to jack back in and rescue Morpheus, confesses he is not the One, and, unable to justify the mission logically, grounds it in belief. Trinity, after her attempt to insist he must be the One fails, climbs into the chair beside him and, as ranking officer, orders Tank to load them both up.

Recalling the Oracle's warning that he would have to make a choice, he decides to jack back into the Matrix to rescue Morpheus. prose_before_reconcile.action: Tank reaches for the plug to end Morpheus's life; Neo shouts 'Stop!' and reverses the crew's momentum. He declares his intent to jack back in and rescue Morpheus, confesses he is not the One, and, unable to justify the mission logically, grounds it in belief: he says he believes he can bring Morpheus back. Trinity, after a failed attempt to insist he must be the One, climbs into the chair beside him and, as ranking officer, orders Tank to load them both up.

events.title: Smith's Interrogation and the Approach
events.summary: Two fronts harden at once. In the Executive Office, Smith moves from a clinical sermon on humanity-as-disease to a private, disgusted confession that he feels 'infected' by the Matrix, dismisses Brown and Jones, and isolates himself with Morpheus to demand Zion's codes as his personal exit. In parallel, on the Nebuchadnezzar and in the construct, Neo converts his crisis of faith into a concrete, armed plan; Tank loads him and Trinity; and they jack in. The event ends with the Government Building standing inert in daylight, then stirred by a dark wind from no visible source.
events.action: Smith delivers his 'cure' monologue to a silent, captive Morpheus, then, frustrated by the failing serum, conceals a knotting fist before letting his disgust surface, orders Brown and Jones out, and sits alone with Morpheus. He confesses his hatred of the Matrix, describes feeling infected by it, and declares Morpheus's mind the key to escaping once Zion falls; he leans forward, smiles, and threatens death unless Morpheus yields the codes. Meanwhile Neo, having decided to go in, demands 'Guns. Lots of guns' over the phone to Tank; weapons materialize in the construct; and after Trinity names the unprecedented scale of what they are attempting, Neo arms himself and asserts the plan will work. Tank then hits load, sending Neo's and Trinity's bodies into the Matrix, and moves to sit beside the ashen Morpheus, holding his hand and imploring him to hold on.
